correctness.rationale: The kernel identities JJ*=min(x,y) and BB*=min(x,y)-xy give the mixed and full Dirichlet Laplacian Green spectra exactly. Hilbert tensor-product singular values give all finite rank products. Exact hyperbola inclusion-exclusion and shifted harmonic expansions yield N(X)=X log X+B_rX+O(sqrt X). Divisor pairing controls product multiplicity at tied ranks. Rank inversion gives W(e^{B_r}k)/(pi^2k)+O(sqrt(log k)/k^{3/2}); differentiation of Lambert W in the logarithmic argument gives the consecutive 2 log 2 corrections. The extracted standard-library checker passed 636 supplementary finite consistency assertions, not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact leading-order results for multivariate mixed-Sobolev embedding and general tensor-power sequences were compared with the new fixed-dimension three-boundary classification. They do not by implication determine the constant-order correction, the Lambert remainder, or the nonvanishing 2 log 2 difference at rank n; a common first-order asymptotic cannot fix the two-term gap. The classical Green spectra, tensor singular-product rule, and divisor hyperbola identity are credited. Searches of comparable operator models and mathematical records did not find a directly covering theorem. A shifted-divisor or Brownian covariance formulation remains a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: A classical shifted-divisor hyperbola asymptotic or Brownian pillow covariance-eigenvalue result could yield an equivalent correction under different terminology; independent priority verification is needed.

value.rationale: Mixed derivative Hilbert embeddings on the square are natural optimal linear-approximation objects. One-sided versus two-sided trace pinning leaves the leading log(k)/k decay unchanged but produces a nonzero exact n-scaled difference. The full three-case boundary classification, with an effective Lambert approximation and a provably smaller remainder, supplies a precise stability invariant beyond generic hyperbolic-cross asymptotics. It is not merely a changed normalization: each boundary changes a true approximation-number difference by 2 log 2.
